name: Blue to Purple Progression
description: Technical development and belt recognition, explained through Stephan Kesting’s positional framework and IBJJF graduation rules.
summary: A broader technical repertoire and eligibility for belt recognition are separate parts of progression.
overview:
Technical breadth includes what happens on both sides of a position. Stephan Kesting’s Roadmap separates submissions, top transitions and bottom transitions: for closed guard, that includes passing from top and sweeping from bottom. His examples describe a personal repertoire, not a compulsory purple-belt syllabus.

Promotion is a separate decision. The IBJJF graduation rules leave its timing to the professor while setting minimum periods and exceptions for recognition. Completing a minimum period does not itself establish readiness for the next belt.

fits: You want to understand the difference between developing a broader game and meeting belt-recognition requirements.

includes: Kesting’s distinction between submissions, top transitions and bottom transitions across positions.
Professor discretion, minimum recognition periods and exceptions in the IBJJF graduation system.
limits: These sources do not define a universal purple-belt technical examination.
The IBJJF provisions concern recognition; they are not a promised promotion timetable.

sources.title: A Roadmap for Brazilian Jiu-jitsu — Stephan Kesting

sources.title: IBJJF General System of Graduation
sources.note: Read Article 3: recognition depends on applicable minimum periods and exceptions; promotion timing remains at the professor’s discretion. These are recognition rules, not a technical syllabus.

flashcards.question: Does completing an IBJJF minimum belt period automatically entitle a student to promotion?
flashcards.answer: No. Article 3.2.2 leaves promotion timing to the professor while requiring applicable minimum periods for IBJJF recognition.
